review: 514.2-1: B's library was empty while the base variant continues into B's turn, so B would lose at its draw step before casting the second Shock; gave B a one-card library.
514.3a-1: the draw_in_response variant made A discard two cards in the second cleanup step without a fixed choice; added a decision that A always discards Mountains.

scenarios.title: The active player discards down to maximum hand size in the cleanup step

setup.notes: A is the active player and has eight cards in hand. B has nine cards in hand but it is not B's turn. Neither player has a maximum-hand-size modifier unless a variant adds one.

decisions: The cleanup step begins; A discards one Mountain, which is A's choice, to reach seven cards (base variant).

variants.label: eight_cards
variants.expected: A discards 1 card: one Mountain moves from A's hand to A's graveyard and A has 7 cards in hand. B, not the active player, discards nothing and keeps 9 cards.

variants.label: seven_cards
variants.delta: A has seven Mountains in hand instead of eight.
variants.expected: A discards nothing: A has 7 cards in hand and an empty graveyard. B still keeps 9 cards.

variants.label: no_maximum
variants.delta: A controls Spellbook (no maximum hand size) on the battlefield, with eight cards in hand.
variants.expected: A discards nothing and keeps 8 cards in hand.

scenarios.forge_notes: Spellbook is added to A's battlefield only in the no_maximum variant.

scenarios.title: Damage marked on permanents is removed in the cleanup step

setup.notes: Hill Giant (3/3) has been under A's control since before this turn. B's library holds one card so that B's draw step does not lose B the game.

decisions: B casts Shock targeting Hill Giant, tapping a Mountain; it resolves.
Both players pass until the next turn: the turn ends, cleanup happens and B's turn begins (base variant).
In B's first main phase, B untaps and casts the second Shock targeting Hill Giant, tapping a Mountain; it resolves.

variants.label: next_turn
variants.expected: The first Shock leaves Hill Giant with 2 damage marked. At cleanup the damage is removed, so after the second Shock Hill Giant has only 2 damage marked and stays on the battlefield.

variants.label: same_turn
variants.delta: B casts the second Shock in the same main phase, right after the first resolves, tapping the other Mountain.
variants.expected: No cleanup has happened between the Shocks, so Hill Giant has 4 damage marked and moves to A's graveyard.

scenarios.title: Damage removal and the end of 'until end of turn' effects happen simultaneously in the cleanup step

setup.notes: Grizzly Bears has been under A's control since before this turn.

decisions: A casts Giant Growth targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Forest; it resolves and Grizzly Bears is 5/5 until end of turn.
B casts Shock targeting Grizzly Bears and it resolves, then B casts the second Shock targeting Grizzly Bears and it resolves.
Both players pass priority in succession; the end step ends and cleanup happens.

variants.label: giant_growth
variants.expected: After the two Shocks Grizzly Bears (5/5) has 4 damage marked and survives. At cleanup the damage is removed and Giant Growth ends at the same time, so Grizzly Bears never has lethal damage: it stays on the battlefield as an undamaged 2/2.

variants.label: counters
variants.delta: Grizzly Bears starts with three +1/+1 counters, and A does not cast Giant Growth.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears (5/5) survives the two Shocks with 4 damage marked. At cleanup the damage is removed but the counters stay, so it is an undamaged 5/5.

scenarios.title: A trigger waiting in the cleanup step is put on the stack, players get priority and another cleanup step begins

setup.notes: A is the active player and has eight cards in hand. Megrim: whenever an opponent discards a card, it deals 2 damage to that player.

decisions: Whenever A must discard in a cleanup step, A discards Mountains.
The cleanup step begins; A discards one Mountain to reach seven cards. Megrim triggers.
A receives priority with Megrim's trigger on the stack and passes; B passes; the trigger resolves (base variant).
With the stack empty and both players having passed in succession, another cleanup step begins.

variants.label: discard_triggers
variants.expected: Megrim's trigger is put on the stack and A gets priority in the cleanup step. It resolves: A takes 2 damage (18). A has 7 cards, so the second cleanup step has no discard and the turn ends.

variants.label: no_discard
variants.delta: A has seven cards in hand: six Mountains and Ancestral Recall.
variants.expected: Nothing is discarded, Megrim does not trigger, no player gets priority in the cleanup step and A stays at 20 life.

variants.label: draw_in_response
variants.delta: With Megrim's trigger on the stack, A casts Ancestral Recall on itself (tapping Island) and it resolves before the trigger.
variants.expected: A draws 3 cards (9 in hand). The trigger resolves (A at 18). The next cleanup step makes A discard 2 Mountains, which trigger Megrim twice: both triggers resolve (A at 14), and a final cleanup step finds 7 cards and ends the turn.

scenarios.forge_notes: Cleanup priority is an exception in Forge; confirm the repeated cleanup step is reached.
